description:
Check that a number you are about to state appears in a filing, however it is written.

Every number is compared as its digits alone (separators, decimal point, sign, $ and %
dropped, zeros trimmed): "416,161", "416.161" and "416,161,000" are all 416161. Your
figure must be one of the filing's numbers times a power of ten, allowing for rounding
to the digits you give: "$416.2 billion" matches 416,161 (in millions), "75%" matches
"75.0 %". Searches every document in the filing (main document and
exhibits) unless filename is given. Candidates are ranked by exactness and by your
label's words appearing in the number's row label or lead-in text.

Returns found, match_count, and up to 10 matches, each with its document, label,
context and a highlight_url that marks that exact number in the beatandraise.com
viewer. Matching ignores magnitude, so confirm each candidate's label, period and
scale from its context, then cite its highlight_url. found=false means no number in
the filing has those digits: do not attribute the figure to the filing. If you
calculated it (a growth rate, a margin), say so and cite the inputs instead.

Args:
    cik: CIK of the filer (e.g. "0000320193")
    accession_number: SEC accession number
    value: The figure as you would state it (e.g. "$416.2 billion", "75.0%", "-1,234").
        A value with one significant digit ("$10.00", "20,000,000") only matches
        numbers written exactly the same way; "$2 million" is too vague to check.
    label: What the figure is (e.g. "total net sales", "GAAP gross margin"). Used for ranking.
    filename: Optional single document to check instead of the whole filing
name: verify_figure
title: Verify a Figure
